title: Infrastructural Plans for Increased Reliance on Low-carbon Hydrogen Fuel
what_it_is: Infrastructural Plans for Increased Reliance on Low-carbon Hydrogen Fuel

sections.label: Phased hydrogen adoption approach
sections.summary: Singapore will take a phased approach to low-carbon hydrogen, starting with small-scale pathfinder projects in importing, storage, distribution and handling to build skills and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Given the strong momentum, low-carbon hydrogen is showing increasing potential to be a broad-based decarbonisation pathway for Singapore, especially for our power sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, there still remain uncertainties in its technological as well as supply chain development, and we will take a phased approach towards its adoption, including pacing significant investments in public infrastructure, accordingly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Our immediate priority is to start gaining experience in the importing, storage, distribution and handling of hydrogen through small-scale pathfinder projects because these will help our industry, workers as well as the Government build up skills and capabilities to design infrastructure in a way that is safe, land efficient as well as scalable.

sections.label: Hydrogen could supply half power
sections.summary: The Government announced that hydrogen could supply up to half of Singapore's power needs by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government recently also announced that hydrogen could supply up to half of our power needs by 2050.

sections.label: Hydrogen 50% power by 2050
sections.summary: Singapore's hydrogen strategy envisions hydrogen contributing up to 50% of power needs by 2050 if technological advancements materialise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In our strategy for the use of hydrogen, we envision, like what Dr Lim mentioned, that this fuel, hydrogen, has the potential to contribute up to 50% of Singapore's power needs by 2050, if technological advancements materialise.

sections.label: No hydrogen adoption targets yet
sections.summary: Singapore will take a phased approach, has not set hydrogen adoption targets, and will focus on importing, storage, distribution and safe handling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We will take a very phased approach towards adoption, bearing in mind the cost – not just the cost of transporting, but also storing and distributing – and including placing a significant investment in our public infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Therefore, we have, yet, to set the targets for the adoption of low-carbon hydrogen at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: But for the time being, we will focus on taking very concrete steps in the near term to build up our skills, capabilities as well as our experience in four key areas: importing, storage, distribution and the safe handling of hydrogen.

sections.label: Safe, land-efficient, scalable infrastructure
sections.summary: The approach will help design infrastructure that is safe, land-efficient for hydrogen storage, and scalable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As we do so, it will help us to design the infrastructure that has three very important attributes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We need an infrastructure that is safe, land-efficient for the storage of the hydrogen and also scalable.
